newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zinc prices set to rise 20 pct in 1997 -Macquarie.
newsitem.headline: Zinc prices set to rise 20 pct in 1997 -Macquarie.

text.p: Zinc prices are projected to rise by 20 percent to 56 cents a pound on the London Metal Exchange in 1997, and to 65 cents in 1998, Jim Lennon, Macquarie Bank Group's commodities analyst, said on Monday.
"In the light of recent moves, this may prove to be too conservative," Lennon said in a speech to a Metal Bulletin zinc conference.
LME cash zinc prices surged to a 4-1/2-year high of 58.3 cents a pound on March 17, up 26 percent since December 10.

Lennon said that a subsequent correction due to worries over a surge in Chinese exports and concern that higher interest rates may weaken demand in the construction and auto sectors, was only temporary.
Although China will export more zinc metal in 1997 due to higher prices and new capacity, this will not be enough to upset the positive market outlook, he explained.
Prices would continue to trend higher due to a shortage of zinc concentrate production, he said, projecting market deficits of 270,000 tonnes in 1997 and 130,000 tonnes in 1998.
Market stocks are expected to fall below the critical level of six weeks' demand by mid-1977 and by the end of 1998 will be only just above four weeks supply.
Macquarie expects zinc demand to grow by 2.7 percent in 1997 and by 3.1 percent in 1998 following heavy de-stocking of zinc metal and galvanised steel.
